facts.label: Used to
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo para hábitos do passado: I used to hate cooking. Negativa: didn’t use to. Pergunta: Did you use to…?

facts.label: costumava + verbo
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para hábitos do passado: People used to cook on a fireplace. I used to hate cooking. Não se usa used to para o presente.

facts.label: não costumava
facts.sub: Na negativa, use didn’t use to sem d: She didn’t use to have a fridge. We didn’t use to help in the kitchen. O verbo auxiliar já marca o passado.

compare.br: No Brasil, usamos o imperfeito: “Eu cozinhava na lareira”.
compare.us: Em inglês, use used to + verbo para hábitos do passado que não existem mais: People used to cook on a fireplace. Na negativa e na pergunta, use use to: She didn’t use to have a fridge. Did you use to hate cooking?

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: I used to hate cooking.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Used to talks about the past.
After used to we use the verb in the base form.
We say “She didn’t used to have a fridge.”

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Used to talks about the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After used to we use the verb in the base form. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “She didn’t used to have a fridge.” → Falso (We say didn’t use to.)

pages.title: A kitchen in Seattle · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a stormy evening in Seattle. Flo and Ana are in the kitchen. The lights go out for a moment. Flo lights a candle on the table. The room looks warm and old. They start to talk about the past.

“Ana, the power is out! Before electricity, people used candles in the kitchen.” says Flo. “Yes, and they used to cook on a fireplace. We have a gas stove, thank goodness.” says Ana. “My grandmother told me that she didn’t use to have a fridge.” says Flo.
